news.headline: UP's Prayagraj to get 550-bed hospital soon, project completion likely in 2 years
news.story_lead: Park Hospitals strengthens north India footprint with Rs200 crore investment, targets 6,600 beds The hospital is being developed in partnership with the Prayagraj Municipal Corporation under a public-private partnership (PPP) model. Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj is set to get a 550-bed multi-specialty hospital, which would be built with an investment of ₹ 200 crore over the next two years. The project by Park Medi World Limited is part of the company’s plan to expand its hospital network across North India and improve access to healthcare in smaller cities.
news.full_article_text: Park Hospitals strengthens north India footprint with Rs200 crore investment, targets 6,600 beds The hospital is being developed in partnership with the Prayagraj Municipal Corporation under a public-private partnership (PPP) model. Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj is set to get a 550-bed multi-specialty hospital, which would be built with an investment of ₹ 200 crore over the next two years. The project by Park Medi World Limited is part of the company’s plan to expand its hospital network across North India and improve access to healthcare in smaller cities. The hospital is being developed in partnership with the Prayagraj Municipal Corporation under a public-private partnership (PPP) model. The hospital is expected to be completed within two years. “The groundbreaking of our Prayagraj hospital marks an important milestone in our expansion journey. As we work towards increasing our network capacity to approximately 6,600 beds by December 2028, our focus remains on strengthening our presence across North India and expanding access to healthcare in emerging markets,” said Dr Ankit Gupta, Managing Director of Park Medi World Limited. The company currently operates 17 hospitals with around 4,290 beds across 15 cities in six states. In Uttar Pradesh, it runs a 360-bed hospital in Agra and is preparing to open hospitals in Kanpur and Gorakhpur. The proposed Prayagraj facility will further expand its presence in the state. The Prayagraj Municipal Corporation will reimburse ₹ 76.52 crore towards construction costs, covering around 38% of the project’s estimated cost. This will bring the company’s effective investment down to approximately ₹ 123.48 crore. Park Medi World is expanding its network through new hospital projects, acquisitions and the addition of beds at existing facilities. According to the company, six more hospitals are being integrated into its network, while capacity is being increased at three existing hospitals. The company aims to expand its total capacity to around 6,600 beds by December 2028, with the Prayagraj hospital forming part of this plan. Park Hospitals operates a network of 17 hospitals across North India, with facilities in Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, according to its official website. Its hospitals are located in New Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Panipat, Karnal, Ambala and Panchkula in Haryana; Mohali, Bathinda and Patiala in Punjab; Jaipur and Behror in Rajasthan; Agra in Uttar Pradesh; and Rudrapur in Uttarakhand. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.headline: 'People will celebrate': Piyush Goyal says India to have comparative edge in US trade deal
news.story_lead: 'People will celebrate': Piyush Goyal says India to have comparative edge in US trade deal Piyush Goyal stressed that no interest of farmers would be compromised in the deal, adding that India was “focused on protecting” sensitive sectors. India will have a “strong comparative advantage” in the trade deal being negotiated with the United States, Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday, adding that no farmers' interests would be compromised in the agreement. Goyal said that the people of India would “celebrate” once details of the deal are released.
news.full_article_text: 'People will celebrate': Piyush Goyal says India to have comparative edge in US trade deal Piyush Goyal stressed that no interest of farmers would be compromised in the deal, adding that India was “focused on protecting” sensitive sectors. India will have a “strong comparative advantage” in the trade deal being negotiated with the United States, Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday, adding that no farmers' interests would be compromised in the agreement. Goyal said that the people of India would “celebrate” once details of the deal are released. The Union commerce minister stressed that India was “focused on protecting” sensitive sectors and getting a comparative advantage in trade agreements in order to export more. A country's comparative advantage refers to its ability to produce a good or service at a lower opportunity cost than another producer. Also Read | India-Mexico trade deal: Talks to begin this week amid fresh 50% tariffs on Indian exports Addressing the 4th 4th ISID-IDRA National Conference on India’s Industrial Transformation, Goyal said, “I have the courage and conviction to announce that the US trade deal, once details are out, the people of India will celebrate that not a single sensitive interest of our farmers or any stakeholder has been compromised. On the contrary, India will stand at a very strong comparative advantage.” The Union commerce and industry minister said that India, through its trade deals, was not just looking at market access. He said investments and services were also an important part of negotiations. ‘US FTA politicised by few elements’ Goyal also made a veiled reference to the Opposition's criticism of the trade agreement under negotiation with the US, saying the deal was “sometimes politicised by a few elements.” “The US free trade agreement is sometimes sought to be politicised by a few elements. I don't even know whether they deserve any comment because that's probably lack of knowledge, Details are not yet fully out. I don't know what they are criticising,” Goyal said. The Union minister said he had yet to come across “a single criticism” or flaw in the eight FTAs already negotiated by the Centre. “I dare say, none of the FTAS finalised by the Modi government had found a single criticism or any flaw. I have yet to come across anybody who could find a singe flaw in any of the 8 FTA concluded,” Goyal added. India has so far announced FTAs with the European Union , United Kingdom, New Zealand, Oman, Australia, United Arab Emirates and Mauritius. New Delhi has also signed the India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA). This trade agreement is between India and four members states of the European Free Trade Association – Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland. Also Read | India, Canada explore energy partnership as both sides push to seal trade deal Where do trade negotiations stand currently? The India-US trade agreement is in its “last mile”, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said last week while speaking about efforts by the two countries to find common ground on the deal they have negotiated for more than a year. However, Jaishankar added that “it’s never done till it’s done”, while adding that the “last mile” often poses challenges. He said the negotiating teams were working through these, while refusing to elaborate further. US President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who came to India this month for a three-day official visit, have also spoken about the progress in negotiations. When Rubio was on his India visit, Trump said the agreement was “pretty close”, while adding that it “could be a much different kind of deal.” Following his meeting with Jaishankar in Mumbai during his visit, Rubio too made similar remarks. “I would say we’re about as close as you can be without having an executed agreement. I think there’s a small number of items left to wrap up,” the US Secretary of State said. He said the deal would happen “shortly”, adding, “Hopefully we have some good news to announce fairly soon.” - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Arya Mishra Arya Mishra is a Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, and a key member of the digital news team focusing on urgent breaking developments across India and the world. India will have a “strong comparative advantage” in the trade deal being negotiated with the United States, Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday, adding that no farmers' interests would be compromised in the agreement.

Goyal said that the people of India would “celebrate” once details of the deal are released. The Union commerce minister stressed that India was “focused on protecting” sensitive sectors and getting a comparative advantage in trade agreements in order to export more.
A country's comparative advantage refers to its ability to produce a good or service at a lower opportunity cost than another producer.

Addressing the 4th 4th ISID-IDRA National Conference on India’s Industrial Transformation, Goyal said, “I have the courage and conviction to announce that the US trade deal, once details are out, the people of India will celebrate that not a single sensitive interest of our farmers or any stakeholder has been compromised. On the contrary, India will stand at a very strong comparative advantage.”
The Union commerce and industry minister said that India, through its trade deals, was not just looking at market access. He said investments and services were also an important part of negotiations.

news.headline: Denied permission, Opposition moves symbolic CEC ‘trial’ to Kharge’s house
news.story_lead: Denied permission, Opposition moves symbolic CEC ‘trial’ to Kharge’s house The scripted session will see Cong president Mallikarjun Kharge move the resolution against Gyanesh Kumar before the proceedings are thrown open. Opposition parties under the INDIA bloc will hold a mock parliament session at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence on Friday to symbolically “impeach” chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, escalating their campaign accusing the election authority of undermining democratic safeguards. The scripted session will see Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge move the resolution against Gyanesh Kumar before the proceedings are thrown open to other participants.
news.full_article_text: Denied permission, Opposition moves symbolic CEC ‘trial’ to Kharge’s house The scripted session will see Cong president Mallikarjun Kharge move the resolution against Gyanesh Kumar before the proceedings are thrown open. Opposition parties under the INDIA bloc will hold a mock parliament session at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence on Friday to symbolically “impeach” chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, escalating their campaign accusing the election authority of undermining democratic safeguards. The scripted session will see Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge move the resolution against Gyanesh Kumar before the proceedings are thrown open to other participants. Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi will deliver the final speech against Kumar. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar will preside over the mock parliament proceedings. It is not clear if someone will play the role of Prime Minister Narendra Modi or CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Also Read | 'Don't worry about police, lathis': Rahul Gandhi asks people to join ‘Chalo Dilli Ramlila March’ on November 1 Initially, the plan was for three MPs to stage a performance, but the Congress leadership has second thoughts. A senior Congress leader said they had originally planned to invite former Supreme Court judges and jurists to participate in the mock parliament, but at least five former judges refused to join the show. The mock parliament sessions, conceived as a symbolic impeachment proceeding against Kumar, will take place at Kharge’s residence at 10, Rajaji Marg at 3.30 pm. The Opposition said it was denied permission to hold the mock session at the Ashoka Hotel and subsequently at Ramlila Maidan where they have planned to hold a huge protest on November 1. Also Read | Nirmala Sitharaman, Rahul Gandhi spar over Tata leadership dispute: ‘Stop politicising every issue’ “All Opposition MPs, party leaders, eminent faces from the civil society, student leaders and some people whose names have been deleted in the SIR will attend the mock session,” said a senior Congress leader. The exercise is intended to give the Opposition a platform to present its allegations against the Election Commission and build momentum for its November 1 rally against what it calls vote chori. The Opposition has been leading protests against Kumar and has met President Droupadi Murmu, demanding his removal and the repeal of the 2023 law that provides immunity to the CEC and Election Commissioners. It has accused the CEC of the “unilateral and arbitrary exercise of the collective powers” during the ongoing revision of electoral rolls. Under the law, the CEC can be removed by Parliament through a process similar to the impeachment of a Supreme Court judge. The CEC or an Election Commissioner may also resign by submitting a written resignation to the President. Also Read | Tata being ‘criminally destroyed’; no business leader dares to say a word: Rahul Gandhi The Congress last month announced plans to move a fresh impeachment motion against Kumar after the Indian Express’ report on objections raised by the two election commissioners on decisions related to the special intensive revision, but later decided to opt for political programmes and public outreach. Congress leaders alleged that denying permission for the mock session aimed to restrict the Opposition’s political mobilisation, while the venue changes are part of its broader argument that the government is obstructing its campaign. Friday’s proceedings also aim to bring ordinary voters’ concerns into the political debate. People who say their names have been deleted from electoral rolls are expected to be given an opportunity to present their experiences, alongside arguments from Opposition MPs and legal experts.

news.full_article_text: Russian President Vladimir Putin has promoted the country's own satellite internet project. - Published 28 October 2026 Elon Musk is a "real genius", Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday after revealing the two are in "close" contact about satellite technology. The remarks came during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, during which Putin discussed Russia's own satellite internet project Rassvet, which provides internet connections to people from satellites. "He's a genius, a real genius," Putin said of Musk, according to a translation of his remarks by the BBC. "We are in close contact with our American partners, including Mr. Musk." Starlink is part of Musk's company SpaceX. The company did not respond to a request for comment. Putin added that it was important for Russia to be in contact with Musk so Rassvet and Starlink satellites do not "interfere with each other in orbit". "We and our American partners value this mutually, and despite all the political questions, we are working hard," he said. Starlink has launched roughly 13,000 of its satellites, according to the company. By contrast there are only a couple of dozen Rassvet satellites currently in orbit, according to online satellite trackers. The Russian Embassy in South Africa said on Wednesday Rassvet is "Russia's Starlink alternative" and "marks only the country's first steps in this field". "Russia maintains close contacts with the US on space, including with Elon Musk," the embassy wrote. Putin's comments about Rassvet and Starlink were made as the US and Russia appear to be growing closer, even as it approaches five years since Putin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Ukraine relied on Starlink internet in its efforts to keep Russia's forces at bay. But its military last week suddenly suffered Starlink connectivity problems, something Musk has admitted SpaceX did intentionally. US President Donald Trump earlier this month said he'd struck a deal with Russia to import diesel in an effort to lower gas prices that have skyrocketed due to the US war with Iran. Then Trump waived certain sanctions against Russia that were set to take effect. Not long after, a US citizen was released from Russian custody, with US envoy Steve Witkoff referring to Putin as a "humanitarian". Musk was born in South Africa and then immigrated to Canada before settling in the US. All of his business ventures, including Tesla, SpaceX and Starlink, are based in America, with most operating out of California and Texas. The billionaire, and off and on again trillionaire, has been one of the biggest political allies and financiers of Trump and other Republican US politicians. Related topics

news.story_lead: Accused must explain source of excess wealth, not investigators: Supreme Court The Supreme Court rules public servants must explain wealth exceeding known income once prosecution establishes a disproportionate-assets case against them. news.full_article_text: Accused must explain source of excess wealth, not investigators: Supreme Court The Supreme Court rules public servants must explain wealth exceeding known income once prosecution establishes a disproportionate-assets case against them. The Supreme Court has ruled that once the prosecution establishes that a public servant possesses assets disproportionate to known sources of income, the burden shifts to the accused to explain how the excess wealth was acquired, making it clear that investigating agencies are not required to embark on an “endless search” for every conceivable source of income that an accused may subsequently claim. The court said the law places the responsibility on the accused to establish, through credible and verifiable material, that the assets were acquired from lawful sources, as the origin and mode of acquisition of undisclosed wealth are matters within the public servant’s special knowledge. “The prosecution is not required to undertake an open-ended, limitless, or roving enquiry obliging the investigating agency to explore every possible avenue of income that may be imagined or claimed by the accused,” a bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva said in a judgment delivered on Wednesday. Also Read: FIR in DA cases can be lodged without hearing public servant at pre-registration stage: Allahabad HC The ruling came while dismissing an appeal by V Gopalakrishnan, a former Kerala government official convicted of possessing assets disproportionate to his known sources of income under the Prevention of Corruption Act. The court upheld his conviction and directed him to surrender within two weeks to serve the remainder of his sentence. “The law does not require the investigating agency to embark upon inquiries into sources which were never disclosed, never reflected in any record, and never brought to the notice of the authorities during the relevant period,” the bench said. The court clarified that the prosecution must first establish the foundational facts of the case, including a public servant’s known sources of income and the assets, financial resources and expenditure attributable to him during the relevant period. Once the prosecution demonstrates a disproportion between the assets and the known income, a prima facie case is established and the evidentiary burden shifts to the accused. The bench said the expression “known sources of income” refers to lawful sources known to the prosecution through a proper investigation, and not every source of income that an accused may claim to possess. The statutory framework does not require investigators to negate every hypothetical source of income or pursue undisclosed claims that surface only after the disproportionate assets have been detected. Also Read: SC refuses to stay ACB probe into ₹ 2,000-cr disproportionate assets case against ex-PMC city engineer “Once the prosecution establishes the disproportion between the assets possessed and the known sources of income, the burden squarely rests upon the accused to demonstrate, through cogent and reliable material, that the assets in question were acquired from lawful and legitimate sources,” said the bench, adding that failure to provide a satisfactory explanation would entitle the court to draw an adverse inference against the accused. In the case before it, Gopalakrishnan had joined government service as a lower division clerk in May 1971 and was promoted to sub-registrar in September 1993. The prosecution alleged that he accumulated assets disproportionate to his known income between January 1993 and January 2001. After accounting for the increase in assets, the prosecution calculated disproportionate assets to be about 51.88% of the family’s income. The accused challenged, among other things, the valuation of a commercial-cum-residential building he constructed during the period and the estimate of household expenditure. He maintained that the prosecution had relied on estimates rather than actual expenditure and disputed the construction cost assessed by the investigating agency. The Supreme Court found no merit in these arguments. It noted that the accused had failed to produce cogent material to substantiate his claim that the building had cost substantially less than the prosecution’s estimate. A notebook containing sporadic entries of construction expenses was insufficient, particularly as he could not substantiate those entries in his testimony. Also Read: Supreme Court transfers trial of corruption case against retd HC judge to Delhi The court relied on its earlier rulings to highlight the distinction between the prosecution’s initial burden of establishing disproportionate assets and the accused’s obligation to account for the excess. It also referred to the court’s decision in State of Madhya Pradesh v Awadh Kishore Gupta (2004), which emphasised that the accused must not merely offer a plausible explanation for the wealth but satisfy the court that the explanation is worthy of acceptance. Upholding the conviction under Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(e) of the Prevention of Corruption Act , the court dismissed the appeal. The Kerala High Court reduced Gopalakrishnan’s sentence in view of the delay in concluding the proceedings, his age and the trauma he had undergone, retaining a one-year jail term and a fine of ₹ 2 lakh. The top court has now asked him to surrender and undergo the remaining sentence. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Utkarsh Anand Utkarsh Anand is the National Legal Editor at Hindustan Times, where he leads the newspaper's coverage of the Supreme Court, constitutional law, the judiciary and the Union law ministry. He joined Hindustan Times in 2020 after stints at Press Trust of India (PTI), The Indian Express and CNN-News18, and has over two decades of experience reporting on law, governance and public policy. His work has focussed on some of India's most consequential constitutional and legal developments, including the Supreme Court's judgments on Article 370, marriage equality, decriminalisation of homosexuality, the Babri Masjid dispute, electoral reforms and judicial appointments. He specialises in making complex legal proceedings and judgments accessible to readers while examining their wider social and political impact. The Supreme Court rules public servants must explain wealth exceeding known income once prosecution establishes a disproportionate-assets case against them.

The court said the law places the responsibility on the accused to establish, through credible and verifiable material, that the assets were acquired from lawful sources, as the origin and mode of acquisition of undisclosed wealth are matters within the public servant’s special knowledge.

hindi_translation.full_article_text: Accused must explain source of excess wealth, not investigators: Supreme Court The Supreme Court rules public servants must explain wealth exceeding known income once prosecution establishes a disproportionate-assets case against them. The Supreme Court has ruled that once the prosecution establishes that a public servant possesses assets disproportionate to known sources of income, the burden shifts to the accused to explain how the excess wealth was acquired, making it clear that investigating agencies are not required to embark on an “endless search” for every conceivable source of income that an accused may subsequently claim. The court said the law places the responsibility on the accused to establish, through credible and verifiable material, that the assets were acquired from lawful sources, as the origin and mode of acquisition of undisclosed wealth are matters within the public servant’s special knowledge. “The prosecution is not required to undertake an open-ended, limitless, or roving enquiry obliging the investigating agency to explore every possible avenue of income that may be imagined or claimed by the accused,” a bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva said in a judgment delivered on Wednesday. Also Read: FIR in DA cases can be lodged without hearing public servant at pre-registration stage: Allahabad HC The ruling came while dismissing an appeal by V Gopalakrishnan, a former Kerala government official convicted of possessing assets disproportionate to his known sources of income under the Prevention of Corruption Act. The court upheld his conviction and directed him to surrender within two weeks to serve the remainder of his sentence. “The law does not require the investigating agency to embark upon inquiries into sources which were never disclosed, never reflected in any record, and never brought to the notice of the authorities during the relevant period,” the bench said. The court clarified that the prosecution must first establish the foundational facts of the case, including a public servant’s known sources of income and the assets, financial resources and expenditure attributable to him during the relevant period. Once the prosecution demonstrates a disproportion between the assets and the known income, a prima facie case is established and the evidentiary burden shifts to the accused. The bench said the expression “known sources of income” refers to lawful sources known to the prosecution through a proper investigation, and not every source of income that an accused may claim to possess. The statutory framework does not require investigators to negate every hypothetical source of income or pursue undisclosed claims that surface only after the disproportionate assets have been detected. Also Read: SC refuses to stay ACB probe into ₹ 2,000-cr disproportionate assets case against ex-PMC city engineer “Once the prosecution establishes the disproportion between the assets possessed and the known sources of income, the burden squarely rests upon the accused to demonstrate, through cogent and reliable material, that the assets in question were acquired from lawful and legitimate sources,” said the bench, adding that failure to provide a satisfactory explanation would entitle the court to draw an adverse inference against the accused. In the case before it, Gopalakrishnan had joined government service as a lower division clerk in May 1971 and was promoted to sub-registrar in September 1993. The prosecution alleged that he accumulated assets disproportionate to his known income between January 1993 and January 2001. After accounting for the increase in assets, the prosecution calculated disproportionate assets to be about 51.88% of the family’s income. The accused challenged, among other things, the valuation of a commercial-cum-residential building he constructed during the period and the estimate of household expenditure. He maintained that the prosecution had relied on estimates rather than actual expenditure and disputed the construction cost assessed by the investigating agency. The Supreme Court found no merit in these arguments. It noted that the accused had failed to produce cogent material to substantiate his claim that the building had cost substantially less than the prosecution’s estimate. A notebook containing sporadic entries of construction expenses was insufficient, particularly as he could not substantiate those entries in his testimony. Also Read: Supreme Court transfers trial of corruption case against retd HC judge to Delhi The court relied on its earlier rulings to highlight the distinction between the prosecution’s initial burden of establishing disproportionate assets and the accused’s obligation to account for the excess. It also referred to the court’s decision in State of Madhya Pradesh v Awadh Kishore Gupta (2004), which emphasised that the accused must not merely offer a plausible explanation for the wealth but satisfy the court that the explanation is worthy of acceptance. Upholding the conviction under Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(e) of the Prevention of Corruption Act , the court dismissed the appeal. The Kerala High Court reduced Gopalakrishnan’s sentence in view of the delay in concluding the proceedings, his age and the trauma he had undergone, retaining a one-year jail term and a fine of ₹ 2 lakh. news.exam_corner_topic: Banks must compensate digital arrest victims if due diligence fails: Supreme Court
news.headline: Banks must compensate digital arrest victims if due diligence fails: Supreme Court
news.story_lead: Banks must compensate digital arrest victims if due diligence fails: Supreme Court The CJI also expressed frustration over people continuing to fall prey to digital arrest scams despite public awareness campaigns and media coverage. The Supreme Court on Thursday said banks and other financial institutions must compensate victims if the fraud is found to have resulted from a failure of due diligence, and called for preventive safeguards to stop suspicious transactions before money is transferred. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it would examine the Reserve Bank of India's proposed Know Your Customer ( KYC ) Amendment Directions, 2026, which are expected to be notified by November 30 and operationalised by December 31, news agency PTI reported.
news.full_article_text: Banks must compensate digital arrest victims if due diligence fails: Supreme Court The CJI also expressed frustration over people continuing to fall prey to digital arrest scams despite public awareness campaigns and media coverage. The Supreme Court on Thursday said banks and other financial institutions must compensate victims if the fraud is found to have resulted from a failure of due diligence, and called for preventive safeguards to stop suspicious transactions before money is transferred. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it would examine the Reserve Bank of India's proposed Know Your Customer ( KYC ) Amendment Directions, 2026, which are expected to be notified by November 30 and operationalised by December 31, news agency PTI reported. The court stressed that the framework must provide for suitable compensation to victims where financial institutions fail to meet their due diligence obligations. During the hearing, the CJI also expressed frustration over people continuing to fall prey to digital arrest scams despite public awareness campaigns and media coverage. "What kind of person you are in a democratic country if you think you are getting arrested on mobile? Hit the mobile on the wall, and the arrest goes," he remarked, as reported by LiveLaw . Also Read: 2 held in ‘digital arrest’ of man in west Delhi The amicus curiae, senior advocate NS Nappinai, told the bench that such scams continued despite earlier interventions and cited a recent case in which a woman lost ₹ 2.5 crore, the report further added. She submitted that fear of arrest often drives victims to comply with the demands of fraudsters, with some psychologists describing the phenomenon as a form of hypnosis. The Attorney General, R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, told the court that reported digital arrest cases had declined by around 50% compared with the previous year. The CJI, however, pointed out that losses from such offences had still reached nearly ₹ 800 crore this year, according to news agency PTI . Also Read: 21,900 digital arrest complaints registered till Sept: MHA to SC SC calls for preventive safeguards, bank accountability The bench stressed the need for preventive measures, including temporarily suspending unusual transactions that deviate from an account holder's established transaction pattern, automated reporting of suspicious activity and physical verification to establish the genuineness of transactions. "Report will only be post-mortem. What about prevention? Moment a transaction comes, why can't it be withheld?" the CJI asked. The court also emphasised the need for banks to alert neighbouring police stations about unusual transactions involving customers who may be victims of digital arrest scams. The bench asked the RBI to submit a list of all authorised financial institutions by the next date of hearing, indicating that it could issue directions applicable to all such institutions without requiring individual banks to be impleaded in the proceedings. It also sought details of the institutions that would be covered by the proposed guidelines and the measures being considered to compensate victims for their losses. The court said it would examine the RBI's proposed KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, before issuing further directions. From Delhi to Kerala, digital arrest scams claim crores Recent cases reported across India in October show how digital arrest scams have cost victims crores of rupees, with fraudsters posing as law enforcement officials to coerce them into transferring money. In Delhi, police arrested two men for allegedly operating a mule bank account used to route proceeds linked to a ₹ 2.10-crore digital arrest scam targeting a Janakpuri resident. The account, registered in Yamuna Vihar in northeast Delhi, received ₹ 98,592 linked to the case on October 12. Police recovered mobile phones, debit cards and chequebooks from the accused. In Hyderabad, cybercrime police arrested two men for allegedly defrauding a 63-year-old retired employee and his daughter of ₹ 29.17 lakh. The suspects allegedly laundered the money through mule accounts, cash deposit machines and cryptocurrency conversions. A third accused, a Bengaluru resident, remains absconding. In Kozhikode, a 57-year-old woman allegedly lost ₹ 1.35 crore after fraudsters posing as Mumbai Crime Branch officers threatened her with criminal cases and asked her to transfer money to the Reserve Bank of India for verification. The Cyber Crime police registered a case after she received WhatsApp voice and video calls between September 22 and October 15. In Karnataka's Dakshina Kannada district, a 62-year-old farmer from Puttur taluk allegedly lost ₹ 1.31 crore after fraudsters posing as Mumbai police and Anti-Terrorism Squad officers accused him of transferring money to a suspect in the Pahalgam terror attack. Police said he was kept under digital arrest from September 2 to October 6, 2026, and coerced into transferring money to multiple bank accounts. A status report filed by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) before the Supreme Court said more than 21,900 complaints of digital arrest fraud, involving over ₹ 647 crore, were registered between January 1 and August 31, 2026. news.headline: North India getting hotter, drier, South wetter: A study of 70-year climate trends uncovers worrying climate shift
news.story_lead: North India getting hotter, drier, South wetter: A study of 70-year climate trends uncovers worrying climate shift Maharashtra's Marathwada and west Vidarbha, already ravaged by drought and farmer suicides, have moved into a hotter, drier climate zone, the IMD study showed. India’s climate is turning hotter and drier, with large parts of north India changing from temperate to arid steppe and from hot and tropical Savannah to temperate, hot-summer, between 1961 and 2020, a 70-year analysis of rainfall and temperature changes conducted by researchers at the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has found. The study also found that India’s peninsular region (excluding the Central Deccan Plateau centred around Maharashtra’s Vidarbha and Marathwada regions), on the other hand, has shifted towards the wetter zone, from arid steppe hot to tropical savannah.
news.full_article_text: North India getting hotter, drier, South wetter: A study of 70-year climate trends uncovers worrying climate shift Maharashtra's Marathwada and west Vidarbha, already ravaged by drought and farmer suicides, have moved into a hotter, drier climate zone, the IMD study showed. India’s climate is turning hotter and drier, with large parts of north India changing from temperate to arid steppe and from hot and tropical Savannah to temperate, hot-summer, between 1961 and 2020, a 70-year analysis of rainfall and temperature changes conducted by researchers at the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has found. The study also found that India’s peninsular region (excluding the Central Deccan Plateau centred around Maharashtra’s Vidarbha and Marathwada regions), on the other hand, has shifted towards the wetter zone, from arid steppe hot to tropical savannah. Marathwada and west Vidarbha, already ravaged by drought and farmer suicides, have moved into a hotter, drier climate zone. What the study points out The study titled: Identifying the climate zone shifts of Indian meteorological subdivisions: insights from historical records, by Ananya Karmakar, Rajib Chattopadhyay, Pulak Guhathakurta, K S Hosalikar and Mrutyunjay Mohapatra of the India Meteorological Department and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune, is published in MAUSAM, IMD's peer-reviewed journal, this month. The study had set out to investigate historical records of shifts in climate zone modulation across Indian meteorological subdivisions, aiming to uncover the underlying drivers and patterns that have shaped India's climate landscape by examining historical data, including meteorological observations, proxy records, and historical accounts. “Two significant findings came out of this analysis -- over the historical period 1951–2020, the major change in the climate zone is the shift to the drier region, i.e. temperate to arid steppe and hot and tropical Savannah to temperate hot summer for the North West and North East homogeneous regions, respectively. The percentage area transformed to the drier region is nearly 7% in both homogeneous regions. This modulation is mainly associated with the increasing trend in temperature and decreasing trend in rainfall,” the study has noted. “For the Peninsular India homogeneous region, the climate zones shift towards the wetter zone, from Arid steppe hot to Tropical savannah by 15% due to a mainly increasing trend of rainfall in recent epochs,” the study also noted. “But interior Maharashtra, including Marathwada and west Vidarbha, which lay mostly in the tropical savannah zone, which is warm throughout the year with a long dry season, but by 1991–2020 they had moved into the hot semi-arid zone, which is hot with low rainfall, a change the authors attribute mainly to rising daytime and night-time temperatures,” lead study author Ananya Karmakar said. Climate zones are defined by temperature and rainfall, and the researchers redrew India's climate map for successive 30-year periods (epochs), the standard span over which climate is measured, from 1951–1980 to 1991–2020, using IMD's own observations. The study noted that between 1961–1990, along the coast, the tropical monsoon zone, the country's wettest, with heavy seasonal rain, has extended further across the Konkan, Goa, coastal Karnataka and Kerala. The spread of the wettest zone along the coast is consistent with a broader pattern in the study, in which rainfall has increased over southern India even as it has declined over the northern plains, resulting in Maharashtra's interior and its coastline changing in opposite directions. “The current shrinking and expected disappearance of the tropical savannah and temperate climate zone will cause numerous problems related to food safety and local population displacement. This is something that must be taken into account in future socioeconomic development plans for the country. Overall, the results suggest that the increasing influence of the negative phase of the Victoria Mode plays a pivotal role in modulating rainfall variability and driving the expansion of drier climate classes over Northern India. The continued contraction of tropical savannah and temperate climate zones poses serious risks to food security, water resources, and regional livelihoods. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating large-scale climate variability into long-term agricultural planning and climate adaptation strategies in India,” Karmakar noted. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Gerard de Souza Gerard de Souza is a Special Correspondent based in Goa and has been reporting on and about issues concerning the state and the wider western coast of India for over 18 years. His wide range of stories covers politics, crime, environment and tourism-related concerns emerging from India’s smallest state. Born and brought up in Goa, he has a deep understanding of the former Portuguese enclave’s evolution from a laidback collection of idyllic villages that first drew flower power generation of counter culture enthusiasts to its shores to one that has become synonymous in Indian popular culture with an aspirational holiday, seeing the best (and worst) that holidayers have to offer. He also keenly follows criminal trials. Most notably, he covered the trial surrounding the killing of Scarlett Keeling, a British teenager found dead on Anjuna beach, and that of Danielle McLaughlin similarly killed in south Goa, among others. He authored the book ‘Crimes of Passion: When Desire Turns Deadly,’ chronicling cases of romance turning to rage and murder. news.story_lead: Students win Viksit Bharat Buildathon for bomb-diffusing robot, smart glasses The national winners included students from Assam, Delhi, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh A spider-shaped bomb-diffusing robot developed by students in Assam, affordable bone-conduction smart glasses designed by a Uttar Pradesh team and an urban air-purification concept from Gujarat were among the 10 national-level winners of the Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025, which entered the Guinness World Records as the “Largest Innovation Solution Competition” with 287,967 project submissions across both idea and prototype tracks. news.full_article_text: Students win Viksit Bharat Buildathon for bomb-diffusing robot, smart glasses The national winners included students from Assam, Delhi, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh A spider-shaped bomb-diffusing robot developed by students in Assam, affordable bone-conduction smart glasses designed by a Uttar Pradesh team and an urban air-purification concept from Gujarat were among the 10 national-level winners of the Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025, which entered the Guinness World Records as the “Largest Innovation Solution Competition” with 287,967 project submissions across both idea and prototype tracks. The 10 winning teams received a combined cash prize of ₹ 17.50 lakh, while the nationwide initiative had an award pool of more than ₹ 1 crore across district, state and national levels. The national awards comprised five winners in the prototype track, each receiving ₹ 2.5 lakh for their working models, and five in the idea track, each awarded ₹ 1 lakh to encourage further development of their concepts. The idea track recognises students who present innovative concepts to address real-world problems, while the prototype track rewards teams that develop functional working models of their proposed solutions. Union minister of state (MoS) for education Jayant Chaudhary felicitated the winning teams in New Delhi on Wednesday at an event in New Delhi and received the Guinness World Records certification for the initiative which Union education ministry hailed as “a historic milestone for school education and grassroots innovation in India” Organised by the department of school education and literacy under the Union education ministry, in collaboration with NITI Aayog’s Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) and the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), the programme launched in September 2025 aims to encourage school students to identify real-world problems and develop solutions independently. Also Read: CM Modi to PM Modi: A tale of continuity and evolution The winning projects addressed challenges spanning public safety, renewable energy, urban pollution, environmental sustainability and livelihoods. A three-tier assessment process at the district, state and national levels, conducted by multidisciplinary expert panels, selected 10 national awardees, 100 state awardees and 1,000 district awardees. The national winners included students from Assam, Delhi, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh. The Assam team from PM SHRI Kendriya Vidyalaya, Tinsukia, won for “Vadiffuse”, a spider-shaped robot designed to diffuse bombs. Students from Modern Public School, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi, were recognised for their project on renewable energy, while a team from PM SHRI Kendriya Vidyalaya No. 1, Surat, Gujarat, developed the “Urban Breathing Pole”. Students from Green Valley Educational Institute, Srinagar, won for “Guardian Bridge”. A team from De Nobili School, Dhanbad, Jharkhand, was recognised for a project exploring methane gas in the coal-mining region, titled “Dhanbad: The Burning Treasure and the Silent Methane Gas”. Other winners included “EcoSync” from PM SHRI Kendriya Vidyalaya, Adoor, Kerala; “WINDMINER”, an omnidirectional windmill, from Carmel Convent Senior Secondary School, Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh; and a tasar cocoon counting and quality-checking machine with segregation from DAV Public School, Unit-VIII, Odisha. An “Instant Thermo Flask” developed by students of Pathippaga Chemmal K Ganapathy Government Higher Secondary School, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, and “EchoLens”, affordable bone-conduction smart glasses developed by students of Step by Step School, Rohillapur, Gautam Budh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, were among the top 10. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sanjay Maurya Sanjay Maurya is a Principal Correspondent with Hindustan Times, where he covers education, with a focus on school and higher education, competitive examinations, education policy and governance. news.full_article_text: Trans rights safeguards pose practical issues, govt tells Supreme Court The Centre on Wednesday told the Supreme Court that considering protective provisions for transgender people’s rights can throw up practical challenges, with trans women accessing benefits and asserting rights otherwise available to biological women under various statutes The Centre on Wednesday told the Supreme Court that considering protective provisions for transgender people’s rights can throw up practical challenges, with trans women accessing benefits and asserting rights otherwise available to biological women under various statutes. With the validity of Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 separately being challenged before the top court, solicitor- general Tushar Mehta said that he will address this concern among others in the Centre’s affidavit responding to a batch of petitions challenging the law’s validity on multiple grounds. “My reply is getting ready. I will reply on this aspect too,” Mehta said. The concerns were brought before the court on Wednesday in a fresh petition by the India chapter of a women’s organisation called Women’s Declaration International, which said that while transgenders have a right to their identity, they should not be allowed to encroach into the constitutional and statutory benefits available to biological women. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant agreed to hear the matter and asked senior advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for the petitioner along with advocate Binsy Susan, to serve a copy of the petition to the solicitor- general. “The matter is sub-judice before us. We do not wish to add another aspect to it. But your perspective is different. According to you, if somebody is a transgender woman, that person should not have the same status as a biological female,” said the bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said. Mehta said that several high courts are now faced with the question of whether a man claiming to have the sexual identity of a woman should be allowed to participate in sporting events as a female contestant. The question also arose in jails, wherein if a man identifies as a female, if he is to be kept in a women’s jail. Even under the penal statutes, arresting a woman after sunset is not permissible. This question will be raised with regard to trans women. Also, Mehta added that trans people may insist on being frisked only by female police personnel. Sibal said that even the Constitution reserves seats for women in Panchayats which cannot be encroached upon by trans women. “The Act makes provisions for transgenders. At the same time, there are constitutional and statutory benefits promised to biological females. The question is whether those rights and protections can be encroached upon by transgender persons,” he said. He added that while the petitioner supported the right of transgenders to be identified as the third sex with equal rights available to any person, the implications of the rights that flowed from such identification needed to be determined.

news.headline: Girl seriously injured in wolf attack at German wildlife park
news.story_lead: The park keeps Arctic wolves, like those pictured, and grey wolves (file image) - Published 34 minutes ago An eight-year-old girl has been seriously injured in a wolf attack at a German wildlife park. She was inside an enclosure at the JohannismÃ¼hle park in Brandenburg, south of Berlin, with a staff member and two other children when the attack happened, police said. They said in a statement that the "precise circumstances of the incident are the subject of an ongoing police investigation".
news.full_article_text: The park keeps Arctic wolves, like those pictured, and grey wolves (file image) - Published 34 minutes ago An eight-year-old girl has been seriously injured in a wolf attack at a German wildlife park. She was inside an enclosure at the JohannismÃ¼hle park in Brandenburg, south of Berlin, with a staff member and two other children when the attack happened, police said. They said in a statement that the "precise circumstances of the incident are the subject of an ongoing police investigation". The girl was taken to hospital by helicopter after the incident on Wednesday. No one else was injured. The park, in the town of Baruth/Mark, has been closed temporarily and is set to reopen on 2 November, according to its website, which did not give further details. The park keeps grey and arctic wolves, along with other animals including the brown bear and lynx. The girl was injured by at least one animal and suffered head injuries, according to German newspaper Bild. It reported that the incident happened before the park opened at 10:00 local time (09:00 GMT) and that the girl could have been taking part in a special visit. JohannismÃ¼hle offers small group tours to allow visitors to spend time with some animals, with its site mentioning feeding wolves or petting a llama. The incident comes after a number of other animal attacks at zoos and wildlife parks in Europe. A keeper at a Dutch zoo died this week after being mauled by a leopard, and a man was killed by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park earlier this month. Related topics

news.headline: New RSS group registers with justice dept to lobby in America
news.story_lead: New RSS group registers with justice dept to lobby in America RSS Friends’ Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing came just days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat held a major rally at Madison Square Garden in New York A new organisation, RSS Friends registered with the US Department of Justice (DoJ) on August 27 as a foreign agent representing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), despite the RSS’ previous assertions that it does not lobby in the US. In its filings with the DoJ, RSS Friends explicitly listed the RSS as its “foreign principal” along with the address of the organisation’s new headquarters in Delhi’s Keshav Kunj. The newly registered group also disclosed that its work will remain primarily informational, but that it does not have a written employment or lobbying contract with the RSS with specified compensation and deliverables.
news.full_article_text: New RSS group registers with justice dept to lobby in America RSS Friends’ Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing came just days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat held a major rally at Madison Square Garden in New York A new organisation, RSS Friends registered with the US Department of Justice (DoJ) on August 27 as a foreign agent representing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), despite the RSS’ previous assertions that it does not lobby in the US. In its filings with the DoJ, RSS Friends explicitly listed the RSS as its “foreign principal” along with the address of the organisation’s new headquarters in Delhi’s Keshav Kunj. The newly registered group also disclosed that its work will remain primarily informational, but that it does not have a written employment or lobbying contract with the RSS with specified compensation and deliverables. RSS spokesperson Sunil Ambekar didn’t respond to queries seeking comment despite multiple reminders. RSS Friends’ Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing came just days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat held a major rally at Madison Square Garden in New York. The RSS, celebrating its centenary this year, is the ideological fount of the Bharatiya Janata Party. “RSS Friends’ proposed activities are primarily informational, educational, public-relations, and community-engagement activities. news.exam_corner_topic: Serbian shot dead after attacking officer outside Israeli embassy, minister says
news.headline: Serbian shot dead after attacking officer outside Israeli embassy, minister says
news.story_lead: Officers were visible outside the embassy in Belgrade later on Wednesday - Published 28 October 2026, 10:17 GMT Serbian police shot dead a young man outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade in the early hours of Wednesday after what authorities called a "terrorist attack". The country's interior minister, Ivica Dacic, said the attacker had rushed at a police officer with two knives while shouting the phrase "Allahu Akbar". The officer sustained a minor knife wound to the face and shot the attacker.
news.full_article_text: Officers were visible outside the embassy in Belgrade later on Wednesday - Published 28 October 2026, 10:17 GMT Serbian police shot dead a young man outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade in the early hours of Wednesday after what authorities called a "terrorist attack". The country's interior minister, Ivica Dacic, said the attacker had rushed at a police officer with two knives while shouting the phrase "Allahu Akbar". The officer sustained a minor knife wound to the face and shot the attacker. Dacic said the suspect has not been identified, but he was a minor and Serbian citizen who was being monitored by security services as he was "known to be a supporter of the Islamic State". Speaking to reporters outside the embassy, Dacic said an investigation is ongoing, but security services said the suspect had posted a picture of the Islamic State flag on his Instagram. Dacic raised the country's terrorism threat level to "red alert" - the highest threat level â meaning stricter security checks and increased police presence at places like infrastructure facilities and areas where large crowds gather. The interior minister said he had visited the injured police officer, who was reportedly doing well and did not need hospital care for his wounds. Armed security personnel were seen standing guard outside the Israeli embassy on Wednesday morning. Israel's foreign ministry confirmed in a social media post that no embassy personnel were injured and the mission was closed at the time of the incident. This is the second such attack on Belgrade's Israeli embassy in less than three years; in June 2024, a man shot a police officer in the neck with a crossbow. The officer who was shot survived the attack and shot dead the assailant, identified as a Serbian man who had converted to Islam. Wednesday's attack comes just one day after elections in Israel. news.exam_corner_topic: India's Projected Debt Ratio Reduction by 2031
static_gk: Reserve Bank of India (RBI): India's central bank established on April 1, 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Public Debt-to-GDP Ratio: An economic indicator comparing a country's total government debt to its Gross Domestic Product, measuring sovereign repayment capability.
news.headline: India Projected as Only Major Emerging Economy to Reduce Debt Ratio by 2031: RBI Deputy Governor
news.story_lead: According to statements by a Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Deputy Governor, India is positioned as the only major emerging market economy expected to lower its public debt-to-GDP ratio by the year 2031. This trajectory highlights India's macroeconomic stability and commitment to fiscal consolidation relative to its global emerging peers.
news.full_article_text:
### RBI Assessment on Sovereign Debt Trajectory

India is on track to become the sole major emerging market economy to achieve a reduction in its public debt-to-GDP ratio by 2031, according to insights shared by an RBI Deputy Governor.

While many global economies are grappling with elevated debt burdens and post-pandemic fiscal challenges, India's strong economic fundamentals, sustained nominal growth, and steady fiscal discipline provide a structural advantage in managing public leverage.

### Key Highlights & Observations
* **Timeline:** Target year set at 2031 for debt reduction trajectory.
* **Emerging Market Distinction:** Unique positioning among major developing economies in lowering debt ratios.
* **Institutional Perspective:** Remarks delivered during an evaluation of India's long-term macroeconomic outlook and sovereign credit health.
* **Core Drivers:** Sustained economic growth, improved revenue collections, and targeted spending management supporting long-term debt sustainability.
bullet_points: India is projected to be the only major emerging economy to lower its debt-to-GDP ratio by 2031.
The observation was made by an RBI Deputy Governor during an economic analysis.
Global peer emerging economies continue to face rising public debt burdens post-pandemic.
Higher nominal economic growth relative to interest rates supports India's debt consolidation.
Fiscal discipline alongside capital expenditure priorities underpins this favorable trajectory.
The outlook reinforces confidence in India's sovereign debt sustainability and fiscal management.
key_facts: Target milestone year: 2031.
India is the only major emerging market economy expected to reduce its public debt ratio by 2031.
Source of statement: RBI Deputy Governor.
important_dates: 2031: Projected target year for reducing public debt ratio.
exam_relevance: UPSC Prelims: Public debt management, fiscal deficit concepts, FRBM framework, and RBI functions.
UPSC Mains GS Paper III: Macroeconomic stability, fiscal consolidation, debt sustainability, and capital formation.
news.upsc_analysis: The projection underscores India's growth-interest differential advantages (g > r), where nominal economic growth exceeds the effective interest rate on government debt. This dynamics enables gradual fiscal consolidation while maintaining vital infrastructure and social spending.
causes: Strong nominal GDP expansion surpassing government borrowing costs.
Post-pandemic fiscal consolidation initiatives and sustained tax revenue growth.
impacts: Strengthens macroeconomic stability and investor confidence in Indian markets.
Expands fiscal room for development expenditures without imperiling debt sustainability.
challenges: Navigating external geopolitical and global macroeconomic uncertainties.
Balancing fiscal consolidation targets with growing demands for capital and welfare investments.
government_steps: Adherence to fiscal deficit reduction targets under the broader policy framework.
Prioritization of high-multiplier public capital expenditures to drive sustained GDP expansion.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003, which mandates fiscal discipline and public debt sustainability.
way_forward: Maintain strict fiscal discipline while expanding tax bases and enhancing revenue efficiency.
Sustain focus on capital expenditure to boost potential GDP growth and keep debt dynamics favorable.
news.mains_notes: Debt sustainability is a key determinant of sovereign credit ratings and macroeconomic health. India's projected decline in public debt-to-GDP ratio by 2031 sets it apart from emerging peers, driven by solid economic growth outstripping debt accumulation costs.
mains_questions: Examine the key factors that enable a country to reduce its debt-to-GDP ratio while maintaining high public capital expenditure.
Discuss the significance of the RBI's debt projection for India's fiscal policy and long-term macroeconomic stability.
news.takeaway: India is projected to be the only major emerging economy to lower its public debt-to-GDP ratio by 2031.
prelims_facts: India is expected to be the sole major emerging economy to cut its debt-to-GDP ratio by 2031.
The assessment was highlighted by an RBI Deputy Governor.

hindi_translation.headline: 2031 तक ऋण अनुपात घटाने वाली भारत एकमात्र प्रमुख उभरती अर्थव्यवस्था होगी: आरबीआई डिप्टी गवर्नर
hindi_translation.story_lead: भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक (आरबीआई) के डिप्टी गवर्नर के अनुसार, भारत 2031 तक अपने सार्वजनिक ऋण-से-जीडीपी अनुपात को कम करने में सक्षम एकमात्र प्रमुख उभरती अर्थव्यवस्था बनने की राह पर है। यह पूर्वानुमान वैश्विक साथियों की तुलना में भारत की समष्टि आर्थिक स्थिरता और राजकोषीय अनुशासन को रेखांकित करता है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### सार्वजनिक ऋण प्रक्षेपवक्र पर आरबीआई का आकलन

आरबीआई के डिप्टी गवर्नर द्वारा साझा की गई जानकारी के अनुसार, भारत वर्ष 2031 तक अपने सार्वजनिक ऋण-से-जीडीपी अनुपात में कमी हासिल करने वाली एकमात्र प्रमुख उभरती बाजार अर्थव्यवस्था बनने की राह पर है।

जबकि कई वैश्विक अर्थव्यवस्थाएं महामारी के बाद बढ़ते ऋण बोझ और राजकोषीय चुनौतियों का सामना कर रही हैं, भारत की मजबूत आर्थिक बुनियाद, निरंतर नाममात्र वृद्धि और राजकोषीय अनुशासन इसे एक स्थायी ऋण पथ पर बनाए रखते हैं।

### प्रमुख बिंदु और अवलोकन
* **समय सीमा:** ऋण अनुपात में कमी के लिए 2031 का लक्ष्य वर्ष निर्धारित।
* **उभरते बाजारों में विशिष्टता:** प्रमुख विकासशील अर्थव्यवस्थाओं के बीच ऋण अनुपात घटाने वाली एकमात्र अर्थव्यवस्था।
* **संस्थागत दृष्टिकोण:** भारत के दीर्घकालिक समष्टि आर्थिक दृष्टिकोण के मूल्यांकन के दौरान दिए गए वक्तव्य।
* **मुख्य चालक:** निरंतर आर्थिक वृद्धि, बेहतर राजस्व संग्रह और विवेकपूर्ण व्यय प्रबंधन।
bullet_points: भारत 2031 तक अपने ऋण-से-जीडीपी अनुपात को कम करने वाली एकमात्र प्रमुख उभरती अर्थव्यवस्था के रूप में अनुमानित है।
यह टिप्पणी आरबीआई के एक डिप्टी गवर्नर द्वारा आर्थिक विश्लेषण के दौरान की गई।
महामारी के बाद वैश्विक समकक्ष उभरती अर्थव्यवस्थाएं बढ़ते सार्वजनिक ऋण बोझ का सामना कर रही हैं।
ब्याज दरों की तुलना में उच्च नाममात्र आर्थिक वृद्धि भारत के ऋण समेकन का समर्थन करती है।
राजकोषीय अनुशासन और बुनियादी ढांचे पर ध्यान केंद्रित करना इस सकारात्मक स्थिति का मुख्य आधार है।
यह दृष्टिकोण भारत की संप्रभु ऋण स्थिरता में विश्वास को मजबूत करता है।
key_facts: लक्ष्य वर्ष: 2031।
2031 तक ऋण अनुपात घटाने की उम्मीद वाली एकमात्र प्रमुख उभरती अर्थव्यवस्था: भारत।
बयान का स्रोत: आरबीआई डिप्टी गवर्नर।
important_dates: 2031: सार्वजनिक ऋण अनुपात घटाने का अनुमानित लक्ष्य वर्ष।

news.full_article_text: Supreme Court directs Centre to grant war injury pension to Army veteran who developed illness during Kargil posting The bench said the government must go by what its policy actually says and not what it intended it to mean. The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Union government to grant a ‘war injury pension’ to an Indian Army veteran who had developed “rheumatoid arthritis” during his posting at Kargil, ruling that the government cannot interpret its own policy in a way that “contradicts its plain wording” or leads to “arbitrary, irrational or discriminatory outcomes.” A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe dismissed an appeal filed by the Union government challenging previous orders of the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) and the High Court that had directed it to pay the veteran, Narendra Kumar, a war injury pension instead of disability pension. “While interpreting the plain language of the policy, Courts will simply declare what a policy says it is and not what is in the imagination of the policymaker,” the Court said. Kumar joined Army in 1996 As per the order, Kumar joined the Army in 1996. While posted at Kargil between 2003 and 2005 as part of ‘Operation Rakshak,’ he was diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis. After his discharge in 2013, he received a Disability Pension. He later approached the Armed Forces Tribunal, seeking War Injury Pension instead of the disability pension. Kumar cited a policy letter of the Ministry of Defence from 2001, which covers disability arising from “operations specially notified by the Government.” The Tribunal allowed his claim in April 2024, finding that the ailment originated at Kargil where Kumar was posted. The High Court upheld this in August 2025. The Union government, however, moved the Supreme Court challenging the orders and arguing that the 2001 policy letter covered only “specifically notified operations such as Operation Sindoor or Operation Snow Leopard,” and not ongoing operations like ‘Rakshak” in Jammu and Kashmir or “Rhino” in Assam. The government also argued that Kumar's reading of the policy letter would make other clauses redundant and entitle “every soldier posted in J&K to the benefit.” The Court, however, refused to accept such submission. It said that Category E(i) of the policy letter that dealt with the pension and notified operations was an “enabling provision, meant to give the government flexibility to cover war-like situations.” It also said that once an operation was notified, the provision applies to it unless the policy or the notification says otherwise. The Court also said that apart from the Union government’s “oral submissions,” it found nothing to exclude Operation Rakshak. The Court also declined to rely on Army Order 01 of 2003, which the Union cited to argue that battle casualty reports are not initiated in ongoing operations. It said the order “causes more confusion than it clarifies.” The Court asked the government to be explicit in future. When notifying operations under Category E(i), it said, the government must declare in “clear terms” which pensionary benefits apply to whom. “When the language of the Policy is unrestrictive, it is not the burden of the Court to limit its application through an interpretative process, particularly when the policy relates to grant of pensionary benefits. A liberal interpretation is compelling, and this Court has adopted such an approach while interpreting such policies,” SC said. The Court also noted that there existed “continuing uncertainty” over which Defence Ministry rules and policies apply and when. It suggested that the Ministry issue “comprehensive, clearly identifiable subordinate legislation” governing the services, in the interest of “fairness and good governance.” - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ayesha Arvind Ayesha Arvind is a Senior Assistant Editor specialising in legal and judicial reportage. She covers High Courts and tribunals across southern India, and believes that important legal developments do not only come from New Delhi. Her work focuses on bringing significant decisions and developments from the region to a wider audience and explaining what they mean beyond the courtroom. She tries to make legal material accessible by translating legal jargon into clear, readable prose and putting pleas, lawsuits, judgments and legal developments in context. She also looks at their political realities and practical consequences for people. Ayesha is committed to the standards of integrity journalism requires. She places a premium on accuracy and fairness, and believes that journalism's powerful voice must be tempered by humility and a sense of proportion. Over almost two decades in journalism, she has covered law and order, civil law, crime and other areas of legal affairs. Her work includes breaking news, legal affairs stories, online analysis and commentary. Ayesha is deeply interested in the law, court judgments and the Constitution because they shape everyday life. bullet_points: Supreme Court directs Centre to grant war injury pension to Army veteran who developed illness during Kargil posting
The bench said the government must go by what its policy actually says and not what it intended it to mean.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Union government to grant a ‘war injury pension’ to an Indian Army veteran who had developed “rheumatoid arthritis” during his posting at Kargil, ruling that the government cannot interpret its own policy in a way that “contradicts its plain wording” or leads to “arbitrary, irrational or discriminatory outcomes.”

A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe dismissed an appeal filed by the Union government challenging previous orders of the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) and the High Court that had directed it to pay the veteran, Narendra Kumar, a war injury pension instead of disability pension.
“While interpreting the plain language of the policy, Courts will simply declare what a policy says it is and not what is in the imagination of the policymaker,” the Court said.

As per the order, Kumar joined the Army in 1996. While posted at Kargil between 2003 and 2005 as part of ‘Operation Rakshak,’ he was diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis. After his discharge in 2013, he received a Disability Pension. He later approached the Armed Forces Tribunal, seeking War Injury Pension instead of the disability pension.
Kumar cited a policy letter of the Ministry of Defence from 2001, which covers disability arising from “operations specially notified by the Government.”
The Tribunal allowed his claim in April 2024, finding that the ailment originated at Kargil where Kumar was posted. The High Court upheld this in August 2025.

news.exam_corner_topic: UK Robotic Claw Space Debris Removal Mission (2029)
static_gk: Space debris (orbital debris) consists of defunct human-made objects in space, including inactive satellites and discarded rocket stages.
Orbital decay causes objects in low Earth orbit to gradually enter Earth's atmosphere, where intense friction and heat incinerate smaller structures.
news.headline: United Kingdom Plans 2029 Mission Utilizing Robotic Claws to Remove Orbital Space Junk
news.story_lead: The United Kingdom has announced plans for a groundbreaking space remediation mission in 2029 that will deploy giant robotic claws to capture two defunct satellites. The mission aims to drag the dead satellites into Earth's atmosphere, where friction will safely incinerate them upon re-entry. Public participation is also being invited to help select an official name for this first-of-its-kind cleanup project.
news.full_article_text:
### UK Space Clean-Up Mission Overview

In a landmark initiative to address the growing risks of orbital space junk, the United Kingdom is preparing a pioneering space clean-up mission scheduled to launch in 2029. The mission will deploy specialized spacecraft fitted with giant robotic claws designed to physically lock onto dead satellites operating in Earth's orbit.

### Operational Mechanism and Objectives

- **Targeting Defunct Satellites:** The robotic vehicle will approach and capture two non-functional satellites currently drifting in orbit.
- **Controlled Re-entry:** After securing the targets, the spacecraft will drag the satellites down towards the Earth's upper atmosphere.
- **Atmospheric Destruction:** Frictional heating created during atmospheric re-entry will cause the inactive satellites to burn up and disintegrate completely, removing them from orbit safely.
- **Public Naming Campaign:** As part of the rollout, UK officials have launched a public engagement campaign allowing members of the public to suggest and vote on the official name for the mission.
bullet_points: The United Kingdom plans to launch an orbital cleanup mission in 2029.
Giant robotic claws will be deployed to physically capture two dead satellites.
Captured satellites will be dragged into Earth's upper atmosphere to burn up safely.
This represents a first-of-its-kind active debris removal mission using mechanical claw technology.
The UK government has invited the public to participate in naming the mission.
key_facts: Target Launch Year: 2029
Primary Targets: Two dead (defunct) satellites
Mechanism: Giant robotic claws for satellite capture
Disposal Strategy: Atmospheric re-entry and incineration
Initiating Country: United Kingdom
important_dates: 2029: Planned launch date for the UK space clean-up mission
exam_relevance: Prelims: Features of Active Debris Removal (ADR) technologies, orbital decay, atmospheric re-entry mechanisms, and international space missions.
Mains: GS Paper 3 (Science & Technology / Space) - Space sustainability, Kessler syndrome risk mitigation, active debris removal policies, and international space safety standards.
news.upsc_analysis: The UK's planned 2029 robotic debris removal initiative underscores the critical imperative of space sustainability as Earth's orbits become increasingly crowded. As defunct hardware poses severe collision risks to active communication and remote sensing satellites, active debris removal (ADR) techniques like mechanical capture and controlled atmospheric re-entry are emerging as vital technologies to maintain long-term orbital safety.
causes: Accumulation of defunct satellites creating hazards for active spacecraft and orbital infrastructure.
impacts: Reduction of collision hazards in Earth orbit by permanently removing non-operational satellites.
challenges: Technical complexity involved in docking with and capturing tumbling, uncooperative satellites in orbit.
government_steps: UK planning a dedicated active space clean-up mission for 2029 and hosting a public campaign to name the mission.
way_forward: Advancing robotic capture technologies and establishing international operational standards for active space debris removal.
news.mains_notes:
Space Sustainability & Active Debris Removal:
1. Threat: Accumulating space junk threatens operating satellite networks and future space exploration.
2. Innovation: The UK's 2029 mission uses physical robotic arms/claws to capture non-responsive satellites.
3. Strategy: Dragging captured dead satellites into Earth's atmosphere for complete thermal destruction.
4. Policy Implication: Serves as a technological model for global space sustainability protocols.
mains_questions: Examine the growing challenge of orbital space debris. How do active debris removal (ADR) technologies, such as robotic claw mechanisms, contribute to long-term space sustainability?
Discuss the technological and regulatory frameworks necessary at an international level to prevent low Earth orbit congestion and collision risks.
news.takeaway: The UK plans to launch a 2029 space mission featuring giant robotic claws to capture two dead satellites and safely burn them up in Earth's atmosphere.
prelims_facts: The UK mission targets two dead satellites for removal in 2029.
The spacecraft utilizes giant mechanical robotic claws to capture target satellites.
Re-entry into Earth's atmosphere is utilized to burn up and destroy the captured space junk.

hindi_translation.headline: यूके की वर्ष 2029 में रोबोटिक पंजों के जरिए मृत उपग्रहों को कक्षा से हटाने की योजना
hindi_translation.story_lead: ब्रिटेन ने 2029 में एक अनोखा अंतरिक्ष स्वच्छता अभियान शुरू करने की योजना बनाई है, जिसके तहत विशाल रोबोटिक पंजों का उपयोग करके दो मृत उपग्रहों को पकड़ा जाएगा। इस मिशन के माध्यम से इन उपग्रहों को पृथ्वी के वायुमंडल में लाकर जलाकर नष्ट कर दिया जाएगा। ब्रिटेन ने इस मिशन का नाम रखने के लिए जनता से भी सुझाव मांगे हैं।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### यूके अंतरिक्ष सफाई मिशन का विवरण

अंतरिक्ष मलबे से पैदा होने वाले खतरों से निपटने के लिए ब्रिटेन वर्ष 2029 में अपनी तरह का पहला अंतरिक्ष सफाई मिशन शुरू करने की तैयारी कर रहा है। इस मिशन के तहत विशेष अंतरिक्ष यान भेजे जाएंगे, जो विशाल रोबोटिक पंजों से लैस होंगे और कक्षा में मौजूद मृत उपग्रहों को पकड़ेंगे।

### कार्यप्रणाली और उद्देश्य

- **उपग्रहों को पकड़ना:** अंतरिक्ष यान रोबोटिक पंजों की मदद से दो निष्क्रिय उपग्रहों को मजबूती से ग्रिप करेगा।
- **वायुमंडलीय पुनः प्रवेश:** उपग्रहों को पकड़ने के बाद, यह मिशन यान उन्हें कक्षा से खींचकर पृथ्वी के ऊपरी वायुमंडल में लाएगा।
- **जलाकर नष्ट करना:** वायुमंडल में प्रवेश के दौरान घर्षण से पैदा होने वाली अत्यधिक गर्मी के कारण ये उपग्रह सुरक्षित रूप से जलकर नष्ट हो जाएंगे।
- **सार्वजनिक भागीदारी:** यूके ने जनता को इस मिशन के लिए आधिकारिक नाम का सुझाव देने और चुनने में मदद करने के लिए आमंत्रित किया है।
bullet_points: यूके 2029 में अंतरिक्ष मलबे को हटाने के लिए एक मिशन शुरू करने की योजना बना रहा है।
यह मिशन दो निष्क्रिय उपग्रहों को पकड़ने के लिए विशाल रोबोटिक पंजों का उपयोग करेगा।
पकड़े गए उपग्रहों को पृथ्वी के वायुमंडल में लाकर पुनः प्रवेश के दौरान जला दिया जाएगा।
यह यांत्रिक पंजों द्वारा उपग्रहों को हटाने का अपनी तरह का पहला मिशन है।
जनता को मिशन का नाम तय करने में मदद करने का अवसर दिया गया है।
